pairs.why: The two are nearly the same; A's yellow is a little softer, with less of the plastic hotspot, so it sits slightly closer to the real cards' matte-satin finish.
This is close to a coin flip; A's slightly chunkier roll and core read a bit more like the rounded, toy-like shapes on the real cards.
A's roll is fuller, the tape layers on its side read clearly, and its loose end is built believably, while B looks a bit glossier and more like a statue.
B's highlight is a little shinier and more plastic, so A is marginally closer to the real cards' soft satin finish.
A's backplate and knob are smoother, while B has more brushed-metal streaks and is the more textured option the lessons marked down.
The two are almost identical; A's metal and door paint are a little cleaner and smoother, closer to the real cards' painterly finish.
B adds scratchy brushed streaks to the plate and more texture on the door, while A keeps the smoother finish of the real cards.
A's plate has visible scratch texture, while B's brass is cleaner and smoother with saturated, game-like shading.
